subject: Area file from letters to binary

messages.author: e0e146e03b404791
messages.subject: Area file from letters to binary
parts:
Hello everyone,

Does anyone have a script that would transform an area file like this (a modified example from the tutorial) into a binary one we use on Biogeobears? I got an area file coded for RASP with hundreds of species coded with letters.  Thanks in advance!

P_mariniana_Kokee2 K
P_mariniana_Oahu O
P_mariniana_MauiNui M
P_hawaiiensis_Makaopuhi H
P_wawraeDL7428 K
P_kaduana_PuuKukuiAS M
P_mauiensis_PepeAS M
P_hawaiiensis_WaikamoiL1 M
P_mauiensis_Eke M
P_fauriei2 O
P_hathewayi_1 O
P_kaduana_HawaiiLoa O
P_greenwelliae07 K
P_greenwelliae907 K
P_grandiflora_Kal2 K
P_hobdyi_Kuia K
P_hexandra_K1 K
P_hexandra_M K
P_hexandra_Oahu O

messages.author: 95e9261d3e867527
messages.subject: Re: Area file from letters to binary
parts:
Sure, I had to do this myself recently.

Here is the function: https://gist.github.com/joelnitta/68b7212f02a15fee974e51bb9c938a58

Here is the code using it on your example data:

---

# Convert the example data to a dataframe
raw_data <- "species region

P_mariniana_Kokee2    K
P_mariniana_Oahu    O
P_mariniana_MauiNui    M
P_hawaiiensis_Makaopuhi    H
P_wawraeDL7428    K
P_kaduana_PuuKukuiAS    M
P_mauiensis_PepeAS    M
P_hawaiiensis_WaikamoiL1    M
P_mauiensis_Eke    M
P_fauriei2    O
P_hathewayi_1    O
P_kaduana_HawaiiLoa    O
P_greenwelliae07    K
P_greenwelliae907    K
P_grandiflora_Kal2    K
P_hobdyi_Kuia    K
P_hexandra_K1    K
P_hexandra_M    K
P_hexandra_Oahu    O"

temp_file <- tempfile()
readr::write_lines(raw_data, temp_file)
data <- readr::read_table2(temp_file)

# Convert the dataframe to a BioGeoBEARS data matrix and write it out
write_bgb_geo_matrix(data, "test_matrix.data")

# Inspect the results
readr::read_lines("test_matrix.data")

---

Hope that helps!

Best,

Joel

I forgot to mention, it takes a tidyverse-style approach, and requires fairly recent versions of tidyverse packages. So if you have problems with it, you may want to update those by running install.packages("tidyverse").
